summary: INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION OF c_ckpt_tok. I edited nothing; every number below is from a command I ran on the current tree. THE HEADLINE CLAIMS HOLD. (1) SCOPE: I reparsed HEAD:<file> and the working copy of both owned files, replaced every docstring with a placeholder and compared ast.dump -- 'AST-minus-docstrings IDENTICAL: True' for src/ckpt/api.py and src/tok/api.py, so no executable statement moved; `git diff` shows the ckpt change is one body comment plus one docstring line and the tok change is one docstring. (3) BOTH DIRECTIONS NOW MATCH THE BODY, which they did not check and I did: an AST walk of every `tok.<attr>` inside src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary returns exactly {mode, seed_vocab, build_passes, build_bytes, min_pair, max_bytes, dropout} plus {d_vocab_ceiling, d_vocab_read_path} -- the fixed LEVERS READ and WIRES READ lines, with nothing declared that is not read and nothing read that is not declared; src/ckpt/api.py::check_geometry reads nothing off `ckpt` so 'none (this is mechanism)' is right in both directions; src/ckpt/api.py::save_period reads exactly {every, dir}. (4) THE SIBLING COUNT IS FIVE ACCESSORS / FOUR SIBLINGS AND I CONFIRMED IT THREE WAYS: `grep -rn 'def .*period' src/*/api.py`, an AST check that each of the four ends in a bare `return U.Windows(int(<lever>))` with no NotImplementedError, and src/spine/compose.py::_periods, whose own docstring names the same five and explains that the SIXTH key ('progress') is RUN.PROGRESS_WINDOWS, a module constant and not an accessor -- which is why K13 prints periods=6 without contradicting 'five accessors'. (5) THE FALSE-PASS CLAIM ABOUT LM IS REAL: per-function harvest of src/lm/api.py shows `mask_dead_rows` credited ONLY by src/lm/api.py::counters, whose body is `raise NotImplementedError`, while the sole executable read in the tree is `if bool(lm.mask_dead_rows):` in src/lm/api.py::decode, whose own declaration is swallowed. (6) K12 IS NOT THEIRS AND I PROVED IT HARDER THAN THEY DID: a tree built from the WORKING copy with ONLY src/ckpt/api.py and src/tok/api.py reverted to HEAD still FAILS K12 on EVAL.verification_fit, and a clean `git archive HEAD` export passes all 14 checks; `git diff src/eval/api.py` shows another agent adding `verify_mode` to that entry point this run. K4 reads '262 declared lever(s) ... 262 named by a stub, 0 unaccounted for' byte-identically on all three trees. WHERE THEY ARE WRONG OR SHORT, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING. (a) THEIR FIX WROTE A CLAIM INTO THE DOCSTRING THAT THEIR FIX ITSELF FALSIFIED. The new paragraph says, present tense, 'Delete or reword that one sibling line and TOK_DROPOUT becomes a lever K4 reports as having no reader anywhere.' I ran exactly that experiment on two throwaway trees: with HEAD's tok/api.py, deleting `dropout` from tokenize's line makes K4 FAIL ('TOK_DROPOUT is declared and no stub names it as read ... 1 unaccounted for'); with THEIR tok/api.py the same deletion leaves K4 PASSING at 262/262, because build_vocabulary now carries the credit too. The sentence is a live hazard warning for a hazard the same commit removed, and no check can see it (K13 prints 'NOT SEARCHED FOR: ... any shape not listed above'). (b) THEY CITED THE WRONG SYMBOL for the train off-by-one: the 'three siblings' sentence is at src/train/api.py::PROGRESS_WINDOWS (the attribute docstring under `PROGRESS_WINDOWS = U.Windows(100)`), not src/train/api.py::process_setup, which spans lines 190-374 and does not contain it. The defect itself is live. (c) THEIR BODY-READ LINE NUMBERS FOR `dropout` (306, 340, 341, 409) ARE HEAD LINE NUMBERS THAT NO LONGER RESOLVE in the file they shipped -- their own +23-line docstring moved them to 329, 363, 364, 432 -- and the list is four of SIX executable reads (368 and 373 at HEAD / 391 and 396 now are missing). (d) TWO COUNTING SLIPS: at HEAD there are EIGHT lost `none` sentinels, not seven (CAP.state, CKPT.check_geometry, DOM.open_partition, DOM.note_competence, DOM.state_dict, LM.build_model, MEM.state_dict, SIG.encode), so SEVEN remain after their fix and their unfinished entry's 'Six are outside my ownership' undercounts a list it then prints seven files for; and the 23 non-lever drops split 8 sentinels + 15 prose, not their 7 + 16. WHAT THEY DID NOT LOOK FOR, IN THEIR OWN FILES: five declared DID IT FIRE counters in the two IMPLEMENTED tok entry points are written by no body anywhere in the tree (tok.build_pass, tok.build_mint, tok.build_converged, tok.dropout_skip, tok.byte_fallback), and src/tok/api.py::tokenize declares `LEVERS READ: mode, dropout` while its body's only executable read is `float(tok.dropout)` -- a K4 credit for TOK_MODE from a function that does not read it, which is the exact shape of the LM false pass they made their headline, sitting unexamined in a file they own. The new paragraph they added to the docstring ends: 'Delete or reword that one sibling line and TOK_DROPOUT becomes a lever K4 reports as having no reader anywhere -- for a knob whose value this function passes to _segment on every counting pass.' On a tree carrying HEAD's src/tok/api.py, K4 FAILS: '262 declared lever(s) ... 261 named by a stub ... 1 unaccounted for -- TOK_DROPOUT is declared and no stub names it as read'. THE REPAIR IS ONE TENSE, in a file the supervisor may hand back to the same owner: 'Delete or reword that one sibling line and TOK_DROPOUT becomes' -> 'Until this line was fixed, deleting or rewording that one sibling line would have made TOK_DROPOUT'. I express no view on whether tests/ should change; that is the supervisor's call and neither of us may edit tests/**.

unfinished.detail: tokenize's block reads 'LEVERS READ: mode, dropout' and harvests both, but an AST walk of every `tok.<attr>` access in the function returns ONLY {dropout, owned_by}: the single executable read is `drop = float(tok.dropout) if regularize else 0.0`. Nothing in the body branches on tok.mode, and no helper it calls receives `tok` (_segment takes the Vocabulary). So TOK_MODE collects a harvest credit from a function that does not read it. NO VERDICT MOVES TODAY -- TOK_MODE is legitimately credited by src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary, whose body does `mode = str(tok.mode)` and branches on it three ways, and by src/tok/api.py::on_window -- so K4 stays 262/262 whichever way this is resolved. It matters for the same reason their own LM finding matters: an L2 single-reader sweep reading this line will look for a mode branch in tokenize and find none. THE FIX IS ONE OF TWO, AND IT IS NOT MINE TO PICK: drop `mode` from tokenize's LEVERS READ line, or state the read the docstring's prose implies (the 'THE SKIP TEST ABOVE IS DISABLED WHENEVER dropout > 0' paragraph is about `drop`, not about mode). This is PRE-EXISTING at HEAD, not introduced by their change.
